newsitem.title: FINLAND: Top Finnish monetary officials to attend ECOFIN.
newsitem.headline: Top Finnish monetary officials to attend ECOFIN.

text.p: Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto, finance ministry permanent under-secretary of state Johnny Akerholm and Bank of Finland governor Sirkka Hamalainen will represent Finland at the September 20-22 ECOFIN meeting in Dublin, the finance ministry said in a statement on Monday.

Akerholm is the finance ministry representative on EU's monetary committee. Central bank director Matti Vanhala, the board of management member in charge of monetaty policy, is the ordinary Bank of Finland member on the monetary committee.
Governor Hamalainen may participate in a monetary committee meeting instead of Vanhala, a central bank spokesman said.

Some Finnish financial market analysts said on Monday they think the informal ECOFIN meeting in Dublin, where the monetary committee might also meet, would be a suitable venue for a decision to link the markka to Europe's exchange rate mechanism ERM.
Speculation about the timing of a linking of the markka to ERM intensified on Monday after Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen was quoted as saying that the time now started to be ripe for a decision.
Under the Finnish Money Act, a government decision to join ERM would be based on a proposal by the Bank of Finland.

A proposal by the central bank's board of management would be passed to the government by its board of parliamentary supervisors. The central bank's proposal would include the markka's target central exchange rate against the European Currency Unit (ECU).
The government would make the final decision on applying for a link, set the proposed central parity rate for the markka, and authorise the finance minister to submit an application.

ERM entry talks would start once the application had been submitted to other ERM member countries, a member of the EU Commission and the chairmen of the monetary committee and the European Monetary Institute (EMI).

A link is first prepared by the monetary committee, which can take decisions only with unanimous support. If the committee disagrees, the finance ministers and central bank governors of ERM countries meet to make a decision. REUTER
